subject.title: WORKING: All Microsoft Issues and PRs (refresh)

question: Should OpenClaw own a continuously generated Microsoft issue/PR tracker with repository code that can rewrite a PR body, or should this remain a manual maintainer ledger?
rationale: The ledger has demonstrated operational value, but its permanent ownership, canonical surface, refresh cadence, and GitHub mutation authority are maintainer workflow choices that source review cannot resolve.

options.title: Keep a manual PR ledger
options.body: Retain the living PR body as the canonical tracker and drop the committed generator, repository tracker, and changelog edit until automation is explicitly sponsored.

options.title: Adopt repository automation
options.body: Approve a canonical generated artifact after all source findings, deterministic verification, ownership documentation, and exact-head mutation proof are supplied.

options.title: Retire the tracker
options.body: Close the workflow if ordinary GitHub labels, searches, and project views should remain the only Microsoft-area inventory.

recommendation.title: Keep a manual PR ledger
recommendation.body: Retain the living PR body as the canonical tracker and drop the committed generator, repository tracker, and changelog edit until automation is explicitly sponsored.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent current-main work on generated PR publishing and its permission boundary makes this the strongest evidence-backed owner for the repository automation decision.
